proposed_core_edits.proposed: Under normal-link distributional parallel trends and no anticipation, the causal estimand is identified by the observed-law functional \(\overline\Delta=15^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{15}\{H(r_{\ell1},r_{\ell2},r_{\ell3})-r_{\ell4}\}\). On the common-rarity class this equals \(15^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{15}\{\Phi[\Phi^{-1}(\rho c_{\ell1})+\Phi^{-1}(\rho c_{\ell2})-\Phi^{-1}(\rho c_{\ell3})]-\rho c_{\ell4}\}\). Its zero-safe observed-count plug-in is \(15^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{15}\widehat\Delta^E_{\ell}=15^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{15}\{H(\widetilde r_{\ell1},\widetilde r_{\ell2},\widetilde r_{\ell3})-\widetilde r_{\ell4}\}\), where \(\widetilde r_{\ell j}=(K_{\ell j}+1/2)/(n_{\ell j}+1)\).

prose_updates.tldr: Under the published normal-link identification assumptions, the causal crime-free DTT equals an observed-law map, while the add-half statistic is a separate zero-safe plug-in. Globally on the open probability cube, the normal-link and multiplicative maps agree exactly on the two planes \(p_1=p_3\) or \(p_2=p_3\), with a cancellation-safe signed-rectangle factorization. On every fixed positive compact coefficient interval, a proved Gaussian-tail transfer controls the value, gradient, and Hessian uniformly; on the comparable-rarity box the common-cutoff coefficient is \(C_{\rho,\ell}=-u^{-2}+O(u^{-4})\), including both planes. The Gaussian drift frontiers, bounded-count product-Poisson limits, and rational outer intervals apply to the deliberately independent sixty-role split design.

project_justification.gap: Djuazon and Tsyawo's Assumptions 1--2 identify the fixed-threshold standard-normal DTT functional, but their interior theory does not cover probabilities shrinking to zero. Existing nonlinear-DiD and functional-form analyses do not characterize the exact pointwise equality set between the standard-normal and multiplicative counterfactual maps, and one-dimensional inverse-Mills bounds alone do not provide the compact-uniform mixed value, gradient, and Hessian transfer needed for rare-panel inference.
project_justification.niche: The project separates a global population geometry, valid for every \(p_1,p_2,p_3\in(0,1)\), from a comparable-rarity refinement and a fixed-compact Gaussian-tail transfer that connect cancellation distance to Gaussian and bounded-count sampling frontiers.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the global signed-rectangle factorization and exact two-plane zero set, the fixed-compact tail-transfer lemma, and the uniform common-cutoff expansion on the declared coefficient box. It then propagates those analytic results through pairwise and aggregate Gaussian limits, a product-Poisson transition, and certified finite-sample outer inference under the predeclared split-role experiment.

prose_updates.related_work: Djuazon and Tsyawo (2026) supply, through Assumptions 1--2 and Theorem 1, the causal identification baseline specialized here to a standard-normal link and threshold zero; that population identity is not a novelty claim. Their Assumption 5 requires a positive lower bound on the transformed density, whereas \(\phi(q(\rho_nc_{\ell j,n}))\to0\) uniformly on the comparable-rarity box, so their interior Theorem 2 does not cover the present rare array. The fixed-probability split-role Gaussian proposition is proved independently and is an analogue, not a claim of membership in their original sampling class. Pinelis (2019) and Baricz (2008) develop one-dimensional inverse-Mills bounds and monotonicity tools; the global signed-rectangle identity, its exact two-plane zero set, and the fixed-compact normal-tail transfer are proved here. Fernández-Val, Meier, van Vuuren, and Vella (2024) and Wooldridge (2023) develop link-dependent nonlinear DiD constructions, while Roth and Sant'Anna (2023) study sensitivity of parallel trends to functional form; none supplies the exact pointwise standard-normal-versus-multiplicative equality frontier proved by the global factorization theorem. Chen and Fang (2019) analyze higher-order behavior under degeneracy in Gaussian experiments, while Marohn (2001) and Arratia, Goldstein, and Gordon (1989) provide broader Poisson-limit and Poisson-approximation context; the smoothed product-Poisson statistic here is derived directly for sixty independent rare cells. Sachs, Gabriel, and Fay (2026) motivate exact inversion for nonlinear functions of discrete probabilities, and Schafer and Stark (2009) study expected-size optimality; the present rational outer algorithm proves finite termination, simultaneous coverage, and an expected-diameter order, but no optimality claim.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The pointwise cancellation theorem is a population result for every \(p_1,p_2,p_3\in(0,1)\); it needs neither rarity nor sampling. The fixed-compact tail-transfer lemma is uniform on any deterministic \([d,D]\subset(0,\infty)\), while the sharper complete-error expansion \(C_{\rho,\ell}=-u^{-2}+O(u^{-4})\) uses the declared comparable-rarity box and rare limit. Causal interpretation additionally requires normal-link distributional parallel trends and no anticipation. The Gaussian and product-Poisson laws require coefficient and positive role-share limits, Bernoulli role sampling, and mutual independence of the predeclared pair--role samples; the rational interval uses its separately stated finite-sample premises. None of these sampling results supplies covariance formulas or joint rare-event limits for overlapping original blocks. The conservative aggregate interval must include zero in the published 37-treated-block application, so no finite-sample power or field-tier recovery claim is made.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The literal statement that every all-full table with all \(n_j\leq6\) must yield an empty retained list is false without a calibration restriction: with \(n_j=1\) and \(\beta=1/2\), the admissible point \(p_j=1/4\) has deviance \(8\log4<16=8/\beta\). The interval theorem therefore uses its explicit sufficient inequality for all-full empty-list behavior; all-zero retention is unaffected. The global Lipschitz constant is deliberately enormous, so finite termination is a certificate rather than a practical runtime guarantee. The compact-tail lemma supplies existence of a common cutoff and constants on each fixed interval, not numerically optimized finite-rarity constants.

statement_notes.justification: The signed-rectangle identity gives a global, pointwise, cancellation-safe equality frontier between the standard-normal and multiplicative distributional-DiD maps, rather than merely documenting generic functional-form sensitivity.
statement_notes.gap: Fernández-Val, Meier, van Vuuren, and Vella and Wooldridge develop nonlinear or link-indexed DiD constructions, while Roth and Sant'Anna characterize broader functional-form sensitivity; none provides the exact two-plane coincidence set or the complete signed discrepancy for these two counterfactual maps. One-dimensional Mills results likewise do not yield the mixed rectangle identity.
statement_notes.consumer: Analysts can determine exactly, for any interior probability triple and before invoking a rare approximation, whether standard-normal and multiplicative counterfactuals coincide.

statement_notes.justification: The result turns the exact population link discrepancy into a signed drifting noncentrality and proves the compact-uniform value, gradient, and Hessian transfer needed for the count plug-in expansion.
statement_notes.gap: Interior Gaussian inference and generic first-order-degeneracy theory do not cover vanishing cell probabilities or establish the \([1/4,6]\) uniform tail transfer used by the estimator.
statement_notes.consumer: A distributional-DiD analyst can decide for each pre/post comparison whether the Poisson shortcut is first-order equivalent to exact normal-link estimation, including exact and approaching cancellation planes.
